items.name: Wendell "Wort" Kral
items.description: The hardened homebrewer at the center of the tale. Fifty-four, built like a sack of grain with a bad left knee and hands stained iodine-brown. Runs a scrappy basement brew rig he calls the Cathedral, and measures every crisis in gravity points and lost batches. Dry, profane, relentless; deflects grief with jokes. Drinks too much and knows exactly how much. His beer kept the farm community sane, and now his beer is the weapon.
invariants: Homebrewer by trade and temperament, not a soldier
Bad left knee limits running and climbing
Speaks in brewing metaphors and deadpan one-liners
Never lies about a recipe even when he lies about everything else

items.name: Constable Verona "Vee" Marsh
items.description: Forty-something acting constable of Hop Hollow who arrives at Brewster's door with a plea and a clipboard. Keeps order with ration lists, a shotgun called Courtesy, and an unshakable belief that procedure can hold back the dead. Enlists Brewster to lead the raid. Lost her brother to the first wave and will not lose the town to paperwork.
invariants: Believes logistics and records can save lives
Will not abandon a citizen of Hop Hollow
Never drinks on duty, no exceptions

items.name: Junie Abarca
items.description: Seventeen, wiry, fearless, and the only person in Hop Hollow faster on a scissor lift than Brewster is with a hydrometer. Self-appointed apprentice who learned to brew from library books and YouTube videos before the fall. Carries a crowbar named Sincerity and her dead father's last bottle, which she will not open and will not explain.
invariants: Fast, reckless, physically brave
Refuses to leave a teammate behind
Guards one unopened bottle obsessively

items.name: Eli "Padre" Duquette
items.description: A defrocked chaplain turned improvised combat engineer, armed with a pneumatic nail gun he calls the Congregation. Performs last rites over the infected with genuine tenderness and terrible puns. Believes the war is a prolonged funeral and treats ceremony as a survival tool; the only team member who asks Brewster how much he has had to drink, and the only one who accepts the answer.
invariants: Offers rites and jokes over every dead thing
Will not leave a body uncommemorated
Asks Brewster the honest question about drinking

items.name: Big Hollis Bream
items.description: Former regional brew-truck driver, six-foot-four and terrified of everything, with a savant's feel for heavy machinery and a map of every fermenting tank within fifty miles in his head. Volunteers for the raid mainly because standing still is worse. Will cry, will complain, will not quit.
invariants: Cannot run far but can drive anything
Knows the layout of every tank and cellar in the county
Complains constantly, never mutinies

items.name: Hop Hollow
items.description: A once-quiet farm community of grain silos, wire fences, a co-op hall and a single traffic light that no longer works. Lived on barley, hops and small-town routine until the infected began walking the fields. Now ringed with nailed-together barricades, a loudspeaker tower, and a ration board where beer is listed as a morale item on the same sheet as ammunition.
invariants: Farms barley and hops; brewing tradition is civic identity
Beer is officially a rationed morale item
Barricade lines are hand-built and imperfect

items.name: Château Fermenté
items.description: An abandoned riverside chateau converted decades ago into a destination brewery: stone vaults, copper kettles, a bottling line, and a cellar tunnel that floods in spring. Its tanks are still half full and still fermenting, which is why the horde has gathered there. The final showdown happens among its vats.
invariants: Still contains active fermentation in unemptied tanks
Stone vaults, copper kettles, a bottling line, a flooding cellar tunnel
Approachable by the river path and the road, both of them watched

items.name: The Thirst
items.description: The infected fixate on fermented sugars and ethanol. The smell of an active fermentation pulls them for miles and can hold a horde in place for days. They will climb, trample and tear for beer; once they have drunk deeply they slow down, stagger and become easier to handle but heavier and stronger. Infection spreads by bite and by a mouthful of what they carry.
invariants: Active fermentation scent attracts the infected across long distances
A drunk infected is slower but physically stronger
Bites transmit the infection

items.name: The Ration and the Bottle
items.description: Brewster's drinking is the thing that makes him good with beer and unreliable with people. Hop Hollow rations beer as morale while also using it as bait, which means the town's comfort and the town's defense are poured from the same barrel. Brewster must keep his own thirst from becoming another mouth the plan has to feed.
invariants: Brewster's drinking affects judgment at crucial moments
Beer serves simultaneously as morale, bait and weapon

items.name: Who Gets Carried Out
items.description: The team is ragtag by origin and welded by choice. Against them: a town council that counts bodies as resources, a plan with no margin, and the standing temptation to trade the few for the many. Loyalty is measured in who turns back when the tunnel floods.
invariants: Team members repeatedly choose each other over the mission
The council weighs the team as expendable

items.name: War, With Minutes
items.description: The defense of Hop Hollow runs on committees, ranks, medals, incident reports and a lottery for the good boots while the dead press the fences. Brewster keeps being offered promotions in a chain of command held together by a clipboard. The absurdity never makes the danger less real; that is the joke and the horror.
invariants: Official procedure continues during the siege
Ceremony is performed over real losses

items.name: Wort's Voice
items.description: First person, past tense, narrated by Wendell Kral in a wry, profane, brewing-obsessed voice. He editorializes, forecasts doom like a weather report, and undercuts every solemn moment with a joke, then lets the joke land too hard when someone dies.
invariants: First person past tense from Brewster's point of view
Narration withholds nothing Brewster knows
Dark humor throughout, never slapstick about real injury

items.name: Constable and Conscript
items.description: Vee enlists Brewster and considers him a resource she is fond of. Brewster distrusts her clipboard and respects her nerve. Their alliance is transactional and quietly affectionate.

items.name: Apprentice and Reluctant Teacher
items.description: Junie wants Brewster's approval and his recipes; Brewster wants to keep her alive and out of his way. Both refuse to admit either.

items.name: Two Men With Bad Habits
items.description: Padre is the only one who names Brewster's drinking to his face. Brewster is the only one who does not flinch when Padre buries a stranger. They trade jokes the way other men trade prayers.

args.viewpoint: First person, past tense, told by Wendell "Wort" Kral, limited to what he sees, does and is told
args.tone: Wry, profane, gallows-humored; tenderness buried under jokes; danger played straight
args.format: Ten-chapter novel, each chapter headed by a brewing log line

chapters.title: Last Call in Hop Hollow
points: Brewster spends his morning defending the Cathedral, his basement brew rig, from a fence-scraping infected, and finishes a batch he cannot drink fast enough.
Constable Vee Marsh arrives with a clipboard and a body count: the horde is pushing through the barley fields toward Hop Hollow, drawn by the smell of the town's own fermenters.
She enlists Brewster to lead a raid on the horde's hive at an abandoned chateau brewery, and offers the town's last viable yeast strain as payment.
Brewster refuses on the grounds that he is a drunk, not a commander; Vee points out that everyone left is something they were not.
He says yes and immediately opens the bottle he was saving, ending the chapter on the first swallow and the smell of smoke from the north field.
hookSeeds: Vee won't say what is already in the chateau's tanks
Brewster's last saved bottle is the same recipe as the horde's favorite

chapters.title: Ragtag, Assorted, Slightly Carbonated
points: Brewster sets out to recruit a team by interviewing the least useless survivors in the co-op hall, keeping score on a clipboard he resents.
He lands Padre, a defrocked chaplain with a nail gun, and Big Hollis Bream, a terrified brew-truck driver with a perfect memory for tanks.
Junie Abarca refuses to be interviewed and simply joins, carrying a crowbar and one bottle she will not explain.
A practice drill in the yard goes wrong in a comic and near-fatal way, revealing that the team cannot yet be trusted with a ladder.
The chapter closes with the five of them eating a bad dinner in the dark and inventing a name for themselves that nobody likes.
hookSeeds: Hollis's county map marks tanks that no longer exist
Padre asked Vee a question about the raid he won't repeat

chapters.title: Recon at Château Fermenté
points: Brewster takes the team on a night scout of the chateau and finds the horde has settled around it like flies on a spill.
He deduces the hive's true center: a ruptured tank still fermenting, its sweet reek holding thousands of infected in place.
They discover the chateau's bottling line has been run recently, which means someone survived inside and may still be there.
Hollis panics on the cellar stairs and nearly dies; Padre's nail gun and Junie's crowbar save him at the cost of the team's only quiet route.
They retreat under a rising moon with a count of the horde and one wrong idea about the size of it.
hookSeeds: Fresh boot prints on the bottling line
The horde's pattern around the chateau is not random

chapters.title: The Grain Co-op Job
points: Brewster proposes a first brew rescue: siphon forty barrels from the co-op's forgotten lager tank before the infected get there, using a tanker Hollis swears he can drive.
The plan requires drawing the nearby stragglers with a decoy wort boil, which Padre insists on blessing and Junie insists on lighting.
The siphoning works until the pump dies and Brewster has to prime it by mouth, a scene that is both grotesque and hilarious.
A straggler gets inside the cab; Hollis freezes, then commits a small act of violence that changes how the team sees him.
They roll home with the beer and with the news that the horde has moved closer, and Vee's council refuses to release more fuel.
hookSeeds: The tanker's cargo is stronger than expected
Junie takes a wound nobody saw happen

chapters.title: The Dry Drunk Doctrine
points: With beer suddenly valuable, Brewster rations the town's stores and finds himself pouring away his own share to prove a point nobody asked for.
Padre confronts him about withdrawal and the plan's real cost; Brewster drinks in the middle of their argument, then watches the infected react to a spilled pail.
He works out the doctrine that will shape the raid: drink makes them slow, and a full belly makes them stay.
Vee's council proposes using the team as the bait instead of the beer, and Brewster reads the minutes out loud to the others as a darkly funny piece of theater.
He refuses to let the team be bait without ordering the trap himself, and the chapter ends with him sober by choice for the first time since the fall.
hookSeeds: The council's minutes name a second team that doesn't exist
Padre's confession about why he was defrocked

chapters.title: The Hop Silo Rescue
points: Brewster plans a second, more daring rescue: hundreds of pounds of hops sealed in a silo the infected have made a nest of, needed both for the trap and for Hop Hollow's winter morale.
Junie and Hollis ride the scissor lift while Padre holds the base and Brewster runs a wort decoy below, and the sequence turns into a slow-motion catastrophe of machinery and comedy.
The silo's hatch jams; Junie's bottle breaks in her jacket, and its smell sets the nest moving.
Brewster does the loudest, dumbest thing available to draw the nest away, and it works well enough to hurt him badly.
The team returns with hops and a fracture, and Hollis quietly tells Brewster that the silo crowd was not the horde—the horde is bigger.
hookSeeds: Junie's broken bottle was her father's, and she keeps the shards
The fracture pushes Brewster to drink for the pain

chapters.title: The Vote
points: Brewster wakes with a hangover and a council summons in a town that has decided the raid is too expensive.
Vee argues for the raid while the council argues for sealing Hop Hollow and leaving the horde to the county; the vote goes against the team.
Vee gives Brewster the fuel and the fuel only, off the books, and warns him she cannot come back to save him.
The team bickers through the night until Junie says the plain truth about loyalty, and each of them chooses in his or her own way to march anyway.
They leave before dawn with a tanker, a map, and a plan that requires a chateau full of infected to drink itself stupid.
hookSeeds: Vee's shotgun is not in its rack when the gate closes
Hollis has been crying and refuses to say why

chapters.title: The Long Pour
points: The team fortifies the chateau's courtyard and starts brewing at industrial scale, while the horde presses the walls and the smell begins to work.
They find the survivor from the bottling line, a chateau cellarmaster, and his account of the hive contradicts what Brewster believed about the tank.
Padre and Junie run a hose line through the flooded cellar while Hollis uses the bottling line as a lure and a barricade.
The planned flood of beer becomes a flood of beer and infected together, and the trap nearly takes the team with it.
Hollis stays at the pump too long and the courtyard gate goes down, ending the chapter with the showdown breaking into the vaults.
hookSeeds: The cellarmaster knows why the horde was really drawn here
Brewster's hands are shaking worse than the tremor in his knee

chapters.title: The Château Fermenté
points: The horde spills into the vaults and the team fights across the copper kettles and catwalks in a slow, absurd, drunken slaughter.
Padre performs rites between hammer blows and delivers the funniest and most devastating speech of the night.
Brewster and the cellarmaster argue about the tanks while infected climb the bottling line; the argument ends in a choice about who gets the last clean batch.
Junie is separated, then found, and Brewster uses himself as bait across the chateau floor to reach her.
The great tank is breached and the horde follows the beer down the tunnel, and the chapter ends with the doors closed and the team counting heads.
hookSeeds: One head is missing
The tunnel was supposed to be the end of the plan, not the escape

chapters.title: Last Call
points: Brewster and the survivors climb out of the flooded tunnel on the river side and learn the chateau is not finished with them.
The cost comes due: wounds, one loss the team cannot fix, and the news of what the council did while they were gone.
Brewster confronts the town's ledger, pours the wine of victory into cups for the people who earned it, and pours his own into the ground.
He chooses to stay and brew for a town that learned what loyalty costs, and the yard fills with the smell of a new, low-alcohol batch.
The tale stops on a single line of brewing log: a batch begun, a person remembered, and no promise that any of it will last.
hookSeeds: The chateau's cellarmaster has a suitcase of yeast cultures
Padre asks whether Brewster is drinking, and Brewster gives an honest answer

args.brief: Chapter 1, "Last Call in Hop Hollow." First-person past tense, Wendell "Wort" Kral narrating in wry, profane, brewing-obsessed voice. Open with a brewing-log line, then morning in his basement brewery, the Cathedral: he is finishing a batch and defending the house from a fence-scraping infected with a mash paddle and a bad knee. Establish Hop Hollow's decline in passing (empty silos, ration board, loudspeaker tower). Constable Vee Marsh arrives with a clipboard and a body count: the horde is drifting through the barley fields, drawn by the smell of the town's fermenters, and will reach the barricade in days. She enlists Brewster to lead a raid on the hive at Château Fermenté and offers the town's last viable yeast strain as payment. He refuses — he's a drunk, not a commander — and she answers that everyone left is something they weren't. He says yes, and immediately opens the bottle he'd been saving. End on the first swallow and the smell of smoke from the north field. Keep it around 1,350 words, dark humor throughout, avoid gore for its own sake. Introduce the addiction thread early and honestly, not as a punchline.

Chapter 2, "Ragtag, Assorted, Slightly Carbonated." Open with a brewing-log line. Brewster interviews candidates in the co-op hall with a clipboard he openly resents, scoring people on useless criteria. He lands Padre (defrocked chaplain, pneumatic nail gun called the Congregation, performs rites over every dead thing with terrible puns) and Big Hollis Bream (six-four, terrified of everything, ex brew-truck driver who can drive anything and remembers every tank within fifty miles). Junie Abarca, seventeen, refuses to be interviewed and simply joins, carrying a crowbar named Sincerity and one bottle she will not explain. A practice drill in the yard goes wrong in a comic near-fatal way — a ladder, a decoy pail, a nail through a boot — proving the team cannot yet be trusted with equipment. Close with the five of them eating a bad dinner in the dark and inventing a team name nobody likes. Around 1,350 words. Keep Brewster's voice dry and self-incriminating; let Vee appear briefly to be unimpressed. Dark humor but real stakes.

Chapter 3, "Recon at Château Fermenté." Open with a brewing-log line. Brewster takes the team on a night scout by the river path. The horde has settled around the chateau like flies on a spill; he deduces the hive's center is a ruptured tank still fermenting, its sweet reek holding thousands of infected in place. They find the bottling line has been run recently — fresh glass, fresh labels — so someone survived inside. Hollis panics on the cellar stairs and nearly dies; Padre's nail gun and Junie's crowbar save him at the cost of their only quiet route in. They retreat under a rising moon with a count of the horde and one badly wrong idea about its size. Around 1,350 words. Use Brewster's technical brewing expertise as the lens for danger; make the absurdity of scouting zombies with a hydrometer land as comedy, not as softening the threat. End on the count being wrong — someone (Junie) notices more shapes than they tallied.

Chapter 4, "The Grain Co-op Job." Open with a brewing-log line. Brewster proposes the first brew rescue: siphon forty barrels from the co-op's forgotten lager tank before the infected reach it, using a tanker Hollis swears he can drive. The plan needs a decoy wort boil to draw the nearby stragglers, which Padre insists on blessing and Junie insists on lighting. The siphoning works until the pump dies and Brewster primes it by mouth — grotesque and hilarious. A straggler gets into the cab; Hollis freezes, then commits a small act of violence that changes how the team sees him. They roll home with the beer and with the news that the horde has moved closer, and Vee's council refuses to release more fuel. Around 1,350 words. Brewster narrates the pump-mouth moment as a professional indignity; keep the violence brief and ugly, not triumphant. End on the tanker being heavier than it should be — the cargo is stronger than expected, and Brewster realizes the co-op tank was not lager at all.

Chapter 5, "The Dry Drunk Doctrine." Open with a brewing-log line. Beer is now precious, so Brewster rations the town's stores and pours away his own share to prove a point nobody asked for. Padre confronts him about withdrawal and the plan's real cost; in the middle of the argument Brewster drinks anyway, then notices how the infected react to a spilled pail — they slow, stagger, and stay. He works out the doctrine that will shape the raid: drink makes them slow, a full belly makes them stay. Vee's council proposes using the team as bait instead of the beer; Brewster reads the minutes aloud to the others as dark theater, complete with a motion to award posthumous commendations in advance. He refuses to be bait unless he orders the trap himself. End with him sober by choice for the first time since the fall, hands shaking over a hydrometer. Around 1,350 words. Handle the addiction thread with honesty: no easy redemption, no sanctimony, and Padre's defrocking hinted at but not explained.

Chapter 6, "The Hop Silo Rescue." Open with a brewing-log line. Brewster plans a second, more daring rescue: several hundred pounds of hops sealed in a silo the infected have nested in — needed both for the trap and for Hop Hollow's winter morale. Junie and Hollis ride a scissor lift while Padre holds the base and Brewster runs a wort decoy below; the sequence becomes a slow-motion catastrophe of machinery, noise and comedy. The silo hatch jams; Junie's bottle breaks inside her jacket and its smell sets the nest moving. Brewster does the loudest, dumbest thing available to draw the nest away and it works well enough to hurt him badly (a fracture or cracked ribs). They return with hops and injuries. End with Hollis quietly telling Brewster that the silo crowd was not the horde — the horde is bigger, and it has started moving toward Hop Hollow. Around 1,350 words. Junie keeps the shards of her father's bottle; don't explain the bottle's story yet. Let the comedy come from Brewster's commentary, not from mocking the injured.

Chapter 7, "The Vote." Open with a brewing-log line. Brewster wakes with a hangover and a council summons in a town that has decided the raid is too expensive. Vee argues for the raid; the council argues for sealing Hop Hollow and letting the county fend for itself; the motion carries against the team, complete with minutes, a seconded motion, and a schedule for sealing the gate. Vee gives Brewster the fuel — and the fuel only — off the books, and warns him she cannot come back to save him. The team bickers through the night; Junie says the plain truth about loyalty, and each of them chooses in his or her own way to march anyway, including Hollis, who cries and refuses to say why. They leave before dawn with a tanker, a map, and a plan requiring a chateau full of infected to drink itself stupid. Around 1,350 words. Keep the war-absurdity thread sharp: forms, quorum, a commendation for a man who has not yet done anything. End on the gate closing behind them and Vee's shotgun missing from its rack.

Chapter 8, "The Long Pour." Open with a brewing-log line. The team fortifies the chateau's courtyard and starts brewing at industrial scale while the horde presses the walls and the smell begins to work. They find the survivor from the bottling line — a chateau cellarmaster, dry, territorial, appalled by their methods — whose account of the hive contradicts what Brewster believed about the tank. Padre and Junie run a hose line through the flooded cellar; Hollis uses the bottling line as both lure and barricade. The planned flood of beer becomes a flood of beer and infected together and nearly takes the team with it. Hollis stays at the pump too long and the courtyard gate goes down. End with the showdown breaking into the vaults. Around 1,350 words. Technical brewing detail must feel real and load-bearing. The cellarmaster should be funny in a bloodless, wine-snob way that grates against Brewster's homebrew pride, and should plant one detail that matters in chapter 9 (why the horde was really drawn here).

Chapter 9, "The Château Fermenté." Open with a brewing-log line. The horde spills into the vaults; the team fights across copper kettles and catwalks in a slow, absurd, drunken slaughter — infected staggering, falling into vats, singing nothing. Padre performs rites between hammer blows and delivers the funniest and most devastating speech of the night. Brewster and the cellarmaster argue about the tanks while infected climb the bottling line; the argument ends in a choice about who gets the last clean batch, which Brewster resolves badly and honestly. Junie is separated and found; Brewster uses himself as bait across the chateau floor to reach her. The great tank is breached, the horde follows the beer down the tunnel, doors close, heads are counted. End the chapter with one head missing. Around 1,350 words. Do not soften the cost: at least one named character takes a wound or worse, and Brewster must feel it past the jokes. Keep first person and past tense throughout.

Chapter 10, "Last Call." Open with a brewing-log line. The survivors climb out of the flooded tunnel on the river side and the chateau is not finished with them: stragglers, the tunnel mouth, the cellarmaster's suitcase of yeast cultures. The cost comes due: wounds, the loss from chapter 9 handled with grief rather than spectacle, and news of what the council did while they were gone (sealed the gate; Vee reopened it). Brewster confronts the town's ledger — the ration board, the commendations, the words used for the dead — and pours victory into cups for the people who earned it, then pours his own into the ground. He chooses to stay and brew for a town that learned what loyalty costs; the yard fills with the smell of a new, low-alcohol batch. End on a single line of brewing log: a batch begun, a person remembered, no promise any of it lasts. Around 1,350 words, closing the tale at a definite stopping point while honoring all themes: addiction, loyalty, absurdity of war, dark humor, survival. First person past tense throughout; let the final joke be quiet.
